source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Investigate all available data sources: In addition to monitoring records, utilize satellite data, local air quality sensors, and any other relevant environmental data sources to gather as comprehensive a picture of the emissions as possible.

3. Verify data accuracy: Cross-check your data with other independent sources, and ensure that the monitoring equipment is calibrated and functioning correctly.

4. Identify the emission sources: Clearly define which industrial sites or processes are responsible for the excessive emissions. This may involve onsite inspections or utilizing Geographic Information System (GIS) technology to map emission sources.

5. Implement continuous monitoring: Where possible, use real-time monitoring devices to track emissions over time, so you can identify spikes or continuous excessive levels.

6. Categorize emissions: Distinguish between different types of emissions (e.g., sulfur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, particulate matter) and their respective quantities, and compare these against the permissible limits.
